result.summary:
Custom-state perspective on the Mongo amendment: 19 findings (6 blocker, 9 major, 3 minor, 1 nit), all re-verified on disk this run, with three empirical probes run in throwaway containers/dirs.

The headline result is that "custom state" is a genuinely empty concept in this project: `grep -i custom` over touch-full-recon-plan.md, touch-aggregator-plan.md, touch-monitor-spawn-plan.md and inception.md returns ZERO hits, and a filesystem-wide search finds zero `state/` dirs, zero `spawn-ledger.jsonl`, zero `control.jsonl`, zero `topology.json` and no `.touch/` anywhere — the touch-orchestrate state standard has never been exercised. So the "migrate existing state files" item that looks obvious is a no-op that would burn a sub-plan and a gate cycle (CUSTOMSTATE-12); the real surface is the four task folders' events.jsonl / orch-config.json / findings, i.e. R-27's legacy adapter retargeted at a Mongo sink, plus a paths-and-digests artifact registry.

Three findings are hard, empirically proven defects rather than design opinions:

1. CUSTOMSTATE-3 — `status.sh:28-49` and `decision_watcher.py:138-151` `emit()` produce byte-identical `{ts,plan,stage,state,detail}` lines into the same events.jsonl. 12 of 130 lines in the live touch-mongo-live stream are unattributable right now. GD-14's "watcher-wins" dedup rule presumes the writers are separable — they are not. Legacy provenance must be recorded as `unknown` (with two narrow positive heuristics: `agent`/`tokens` keys ⇒ watcher, `title` ⇒ status.sh), and fixed forward with a one-key additive `"w"` field in both writers.

2. CUSTOMSTATE-4 — probed in a throwaway `mongo:7` container: a subdocument `_id` is FIELD-ORDER SENSITIVE. `{runId,key,ordinal}` and `{key,runId,ordinal}` both inserted successfully as two distinct documents, and an exact-subdocument equality query for the reordered form returned 0 (dot-notation returned 1). BSON is also type-strict: `{procStart:10028}` does not match a stored `"10028"`. GD-11's ref union has two multi-field members, refs get constructed in at least four modules plus JS templates — one reordered dict literal silently breaks the idempotency guarantee the whole Mongo case rests on. Needs one `refkey()` canonicalizer, dot-notation-only queries, and `$jsonSchema` bsonType pins.

3. CUSTOMSTATE-2 — D4's `source` enum is a channel, not a trust class (`legacy` is both fact and assertion), so "show me only what the harness says" is inexpressible. Needs an orthogonal `provenance: harness|derived|asserted|touch` that the custom-state writer is structurally incapable of forging.

The other blockers: the mirror needs an explicit upsert-only/no-delete invariant or the retention-sweep durability argument is false (CUSTOMSTATE-5); and the writer topology must be decided as "agents write files only, aggregator is sole Mongo writer" — a Mongo helper inside agents would put a credential in every prompt and stall 30 s on pymongo's default serverSelectionTimeoutMS, violating the already-settled "a best-effort writer must never break an agent" rule (CUSTOMSTATE-6).

The positive design proposal running through the majors: a `slots` collection keyed `(sessionKey, root, name, attempt)` as the single name↔agentId hop (custom state is addressed by NAME because agentId is unknowable pre-spawn, while the mirror is addressed by agentId), with a `pending|bound|orphaned|conflict` resolution state machine because GD-7 explicitly permits nodes that never get a marker; two ref-union members promoted from tail-retained to validated (`{root,name,attempt}` and `{task,plan,stage?,attempt?}`); one `custom_state_events` (append-only, source of truth) plus one `custom_state` (derived, droppable, rebuildable) collection installation-wide, never per task or session; and `.touch/` retained as the crash-durable WAL with Mongo as a non-blocking projection, which narrows the D8 amendment to "stdlib-only on the ingest and serve critical path".

Two sequencing traps worth surfacing to the synthesizer: `touch-orchestrate/SKILL.md:74-76` on disk still names the `.touch/` + task-dir-fallback control path that R-20 deletes, so any custom-state control ingest scheduled before R-20 will read the wrong location (CUSTOMSTATE-11); and GD-15's one-file-one-owner rule means the Mongo sink needs an owned file named before the divider runs, or two sub-plans will both claim `store.py` (CUSTOMSTATE-18).

Provisioning is NOT a blocker — probed and recorded: `pip download pymongo` succeeded through the proxy (4.17.0 cp313 wheel, no compiler needed, host Python 3.13.7), `docker pull mongo:7` succeeded (image resident, 1.19 GB), and a throwaway container answered ping in under 30 s. No `mongod`/`mongosh` on the host PATH. Probe container was removed; the live task folder was touched only by the two mandated status.sh calls.

result.summary:
Read the live main-session transcript (292fc08c, 267 records / 816KB at read time, growing during the run) end to end plus all five sibling sessions, both workflow trees, the registry, history.jsonl, and the three plan documents. 16 findings: 5 blockers, 7 majors, 3 minors, 1 nit.

The biggest structural problem is that this session is NOT the primary requirements source. The four decisive user statements about Mongo, per-session collections, custom subagent state, and line-number mapping were made in session e423cd3c (records 081b28a7, 1ec9c5c1, abe6607f, 70eb3975), and were answered there with a full schema the user has already read (071e7c25, a13ef1b0, e551fdef). This session's four asks (90cd92b1, 761331dc, b003ac9f, 5e05ab4e) only re-ask whether the plan covers them. The two answer sets contradict each other: 8 collections vs 5, `nodes` vs `run_nodes`, `:` vs `-` in the session key, and custom state as a separate collection (the user's own words, twice) vs a subdocument on `agents`. An amendment written from this session alone will silently overturn things the user was told.

Three blockers are empirical rather than editorial. (a) `sessions._id = (pid,procStart)`, promised in both answers, is unbuildable for 5 of the 6 sessions on this machine: the registry holds exactly one entry (pid 15934), transcripts contain zero `pid`/`procStart` fields, and `procStart` is a clock-tick string that cannot be reconstructed after the process exits — GD-6/R-25 already solved this with a historical arm that both Mongo answers ignore. (b) `records._id = uuid` covers 193 of 267 records; 8 of 12 record types carry no uuid at all, and 17 `mode` + 17 `permission-mode` + 5 `ai-title` lines are byte-identical, so a content-hash key collapses 39 records into 3 while an ObjectId key makes re-ingest non-idempotent — the four CLI buckets are named in inception.md but no type→bucket table exists anywhere, and `queue-operation`/`frame-link` appear in none. (c) Records contain BSON-hostile shapes: `file-history-snapshot.snapshot.trackedFileBackups` is a map keyed by relative file path (66 dotted keys corpus-wide), 55 lines carry embedded NUL, and the largest line is 872,578 bytes.

The amendment's own anchor is broken: touch-full-recon-plan.md:27 labels "D8" as the journal-`result` sub-clause and marks it SUPERSEDED, while D8 in the T-plan is the Stack decision that pins stdlib-only — read literally the normative plan has already superseded the constraint this amendment exists to lift. And the Mongo discard plus the stdlib pin survive only inside touch-monitor-spawn-plan.md, which touch-full-recon explicitly supersedes; grep finds zero occurrences of "mongo" in the normative plan.

Two findings are live specimens from this very run. All five researchers are emitting under the single label "research #1" with 8-hex ids while the watcher checkpoint holds their distinct stages (decision_watcher.py:550 discards `info['stage']`) — the exact collision R-13 is meant to fix, reproducing inside the run that researches monitoring correctness, and a direct hazard for a mirror whose GD-11 validator rejects non-17-hex ids. Separately, the Workflow `toolUseResult` at lines 57 and 236 carries a run-level `taskId` (w4hiywrt6, www4dk54h) plus `transcriptDir` — the only deterministic main-session→run join that exists — contradicting GD-8's blanket "stop is unavailable" for the Workflow profile and R-33's `"taskId": null`.

Traced both pipelines end to end (status.sh/decision_watcher -> events.jsonl -> monitor_server -> WS -> monitor.html today; R-23 tailer -> R-26 ingest -> R-24 store -> R-30/R-31 -> R-32 planned) and measured the Mongo dimension empirically against the mongo:7 probe container running in this sandbox. Headline decide-inputs: (1) the live path must be MEMORY-authoritative with Mongo as a write-behind mirror — change streams are unavailable on the standalone mongod this environment produces (verified Location40573), and the v0 server already holds the reduction, so a change stream would only echo its own writes back; (2) when Mongo is down the live view must be fully functional (JSONL stays primary, bounded async queue, /health mirror:degraded, watermark backfill); (3) latency budget is 100ms flush + 250ms poll + <=50ms reduce/push = <=400ms p95, and Mongo contributes 0ms off the critical path (measured 0.61ms w:1, 1.65ms j:true, 37ms for a 2000-doc bulk) — the poll interval is the budget, not the database. Correctness core: persist observations only, never derived verdicts or liveness (this run is CURRENTLY reproducing the fabricated research->failed badge — this task's own research.workflow.js:172 emits no `research plan done`, so decision_watcher.py:646 will badge it failed at synthesizer spawn, exactly as touch-full-recon did at 14:06:23 before a hand-appended correction at 14:21:24; mirroring that into a permanent store makes a wrong verdict durable history, so R-08/R-09 are a hard precondition). Store absolute per-(agentId, message.id) usage docs rather than deltas — measured 133 usage docs vs 217 delta events for the same run, fewer AND idempotent, since summed deltas silently double on any duplicated write. Two verified Mongo traps that would break "deterministic persistence": a BSON sub-document _id is field-order sensitive (a reordered {seq,stream} insert is ACCEPTED, storing the same logical event twice, and findOne by the reordered key returns null) — and GD-11's ref union shapes {runId,key,ordinal}/{pid,procStart} are exactly that shape; and a cursor query on dotted _id subfields is a COLLSCAN, while both indexed alternatives (top-level {stream:1,seq:1} or a zero-padded string _id) are IXSCAN (999-doc tail out of 20k in 7ms). Determinism also needs two different key rules because transcripts are rewritten (performCompactTranscript) while events.jsonl is not: line-ordinal keys for append-only sources, record uuid for transcripts. Security blocker: the mongod shape this environment produces has zero configured users and publishes 0.0.0.0:27017 with an anonymous /data/db volume, while the data being mirrored is the unredacted transcripts GD-13 exists to protect. Also found three live-flow defects independent of Mongo: a never-resulting parallel sibling wedges run_outcome forever (decision_watcher.py:459 plus the strictly-greater-attempt guard at :615 — this run has five same-attempt siblings), monitor.html:334-344 invents a freeze-to-stale rule that a Mongo-backed read API will contradict, and the full-replay-on-connect design (offset=0 + page rebuild) does not survive a shared history store. Findings file: /home/laniakea/Projects/touch/.claude/local-orchestrators/touch-mongo-live/findings/research-liveflow-attempt-1.md

result.summary:
Re-verified the session data layer live against this session and the 5 siblings (6 transcripts, 4 workflow runs, 15.85 MB), plus the 2.1.220 binary's actual transcript-writer class. 16 findings, 3 blockers.

The real tree is NOT the documented flat layout: workflow agents live under `<sessionId>/subagents/workflows/<runId>/agent-<17hex>.jsonl` alongside `journal.jsonl`, while Agent-tool spawns use the flat `subagents/agent-*.jsonl` form; both coexist in one session (dd469822).

Three blockers, each measured not hypothesised:
(1) 74 of 267 lines in the current transcript have NO `uuid` — 8 of 12 record types. GD-11's ref union leads with `{uuid}` and R-26 keys records by it, so a Mongo unique index drops/collides on 28% of every transcript. Two distinct semantics are conflated: idempotent last-wins state re-appended every ≥32 KiB (`mode` 17 copies/1 value, `permission-mode` 17/1, `ai-title` 5/1) vs genuine log lines (`last-prompt` 16/16, `queue-operation`, `frame-link`, `file-history-delta`). None carry a timestamp.
(2) The transcript is not append-only. `performRemoveByUuid` opens `r+`, truncates at the target line and rewrites the tail (full-file rewrite fallback below 50 MiB); `performCompactTranscript` whole-file rewrites above 20 MiB, gated by a flag set at runtime via `EVs(kCm())`. R-23's `(st_dev,st_ino,size,offset)` checkpoint correctly detects this and transfers unchanged — but "idempotent re-ingest" in a DB means upsert, and upsert never deletes, so tombstoned records survive forever. Needs a mark-and-sweep `ingestGeneration`.
(3) `/clear` at 03:16:16 split run wf_829e6f58-b2f across two session dirs: the journal and 6 agent files stayed under dd469822 (journal still appended at 03:26, ten minutes after the split), while the tail of the in-flight agent a2fc883c96ff7b837, a brand-new agent, and the run snapshot went to e423cd3c. That agent is 223 lines + 2 lines; the fragment's `sessionId` was rewritten to the new session and it has no `.meta.json`. The only stitch is `parentUuid` = the other fragment's last `uuid` (verified exactly). So `sessionId` is not a valid grouping key for agent records, and run discovery must glob across sessions.

Also: journal records carry no timestamp at all (ordering only); `<runId>.json` is terminal-only (the live run has none); snapshot `agentCount` is the distinct-node count (6) not the started count (9); `wf_455b348c-e17` proves key-reuse on replay (3 keys re-run with new agentIds after an abort), which pins the missing `ordinal` derivation and shows that started-without-result must never render as "running"; token dedup by `message.id` is re-confirmed (2.57x main, 2.4x agent) but must become upserted docs rather than `$inc`; max single line is 877 KB, forcing one-doc-per-record under the 16 MiB BSON cap.

The report is written amendment-style: every touched item states its disposition by id (R-23 transfers unchanged +1 clause; R-25 and R-26 amended in five places each; D6 stands; GD-7/GD-10/GD-11 extended), plus a consolidated S1–S9 source/checkpoint/trigger/ordering table. Note for the synthesizer: D8's stdlib-only rule cannot survive a MongoDB sink (pymongo still not importable; a mongo:7 container is now running) and needs an explicit AMENDED disposition.

result.summary: MongoDB-layer research, all claims probed empirically in /tmp/claude-1000 against a live mongo:7 container. FEASIBILITY: pip install pymongo works (4.17.0); no mongod binary and no apt candidate, but `docker pull mongo:7` succeeds through the proxy and the container runs (server 7.0.39, wire 21) — so Mongo is deployable here today. Decisively, D8 (stdlib-only) need NOT be broken: I wrote a ~90-line stdlib BSON + OP_MSG client on a raw socket and it performed hello/insert/update-$max/find/createIndexes with ok:1, so "adopt Mongo" and "take a dependency" are separable, costed choices (MONGOSCHEMA-5). THREE BLOCKERS found by probing the corpus (all 50 jsonl under ~/.claude/projects, 3793 records): (1) 333 records (8.8%) carry NO uuid, so GD-11/D3's "records keyed by uuid" has no arm for them, and the obvious content-hash fallback silently loses 142 of 333 — `mode`/`permission-mode`/`ai-title` lines recur byte-identically dozens of times per session; (2) `output_tokens` GROWS across the split records of one message.id (571 of 901 message.ids differ; first-wins 381k vs last-wins/$max 1,054k vs naive-sum 1,436k), which falsifies inception.md:78's "usage is copied onto every split record" and makes a `$set` last-wins upsert order-dependent — `$max` per field is the fix and was verified stable across randomly shuffled passes; (3) change streams fail on a standalone mongod (OperationFailure 40573), so Mongo cannot be the liveness path for requirement 3 — capped-collection tailable cursors DO work on standalone and are the only no-topology-change push option.
